answer.evidence: The candidate is a seamless 96x80 flat ground texture filling the whole canvas. Dark seam lines run horizontally (rows 3, 18, 33, 50, 67) and vertically, forming irregular pads. Cracks and brownish chunk holes are scattered across the field. No standing volume is drawn: no front face, no eave line, no ellipse, and no side face. It is a flat terrain tile viewed top-down, as the terrain kind requires, so it has no front face by design.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate matches the paving reference on the primary facts: 7 visible tones per tile against 7, and 0% near-flat coverage like both references. Only 22% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the seams and cracks lean tinted (dark purple-grey and brown) rather than black. The reference paving is 80% neutral. The pads show about 6 lightness steps: highlight edge, light, mid, speckle, dark crack and deep seam. Texture is present throughout as grain speckle, rust-brown stains, hairline cracks and chipped pad corners. The seams carry a light bevel line. No area reaches 5x5 flat fill. Only 10 distinct colours in total is modest, but the visible density is at the reference level. Cracks cross tile borders and the pads repeat plausibly. The 4x3 board reads as a coherent ground patch, not a sticker.
